How to use the pool volume calculator

  1. Pick the shape: rectangle, round or oval.
  2. Enter the inside length and width, or the diameter for a round pool (the full width across, not the radius).
  3. Choose a constant depth, or enter the shallow end and the deep end; the calculator uses the average depth.
  4. Optional: enter your hose or pump flow rate to see the fill time.

Formulas

  • Rectangle: volume = length × width × average depth.
  • Round: volume = π ÷ 4 × diameter² × average depth.
  • Oval: this calculator treats an oval as an ellipse: volume = π ÷ 4 × length × width × average depth. Many above-ground "oval" pools have two straight sides; they hold more water than an ellipse of the same length and width (about 14 % more for a 15 × 30 ft pool), so measure them as a rectangle plus a round pool.
  • Average depth = (shallow end + deep end) ÷ 2. Units: 1 ft³ = 7.48052 US gallons; 1 m³ = 1000 liters; 1 US gallon = 3.785411784 liters.

Example: a 16 × 32 ft rectangular pool, 3 ft deep at the shallow end and 8 ft at the deep end: average depth 5.5 ft, volume 16 × 32 × 5.5 = 2,816 ft³ = 21,065 US gallons (79.7 m³). A round pool 24 ft across and 4 ft deep holds 1,810 ft³ = 13,536 gallons. At 10 gal/min, the rectangular pool takes about 35.1 hours to fill.

Example: an 8 × 4 m rectangular pool, 1.2 m deep at the shallow end and 1.8 m at the deep end: average depth 1.5 m, volume 8 × 4 × 1.5 = 48 m³ = 48,000 liters (12,680 US gallons). At 30 L/min it takes about 26.7 hours (26:40) to fill.

Tips

  • Measure the water line, not the coping: water usually sits a few inches below the top.
  • Freeform and kidney pools are not covered because there is no sourced formula for them; split them into rectangles and circles.
  • Use the volume from this page when a product label asks for your pool size, and follow the label for doses.

Sources

Gallon and liter conversions: NIST Handbook 44, Appendix C (1 US gallon = 231 in³).

FAQ

How many gallons are in my pool?

Multiply length × width × average depth to get cubic feet, then multiply by 7.48052 for US gallons.cubic meters, then multiply by 1000 for liters (or by 264.172 for US gallons).

How do I measure a round pool?

Measure the diameter: the full distance across the pool through the center. Entering the radius instead would give a volume four times too small.

What formula is used for an oval pool?

An ellipse: π ÷ 4 × length × width × depth. Oval pools with straight sides hold more water, so treat the straight section as a rectangle and the two ends as one round pool.

How long will it take to fill my pool?

Divide the volume by the flow rate. A 21,065-gallon pool at 10 gal/min takes about 35.1 hours.A 48,000-liter pool at 30 L/min takes about 26.7 hours. Check your water company's rules before filling a large pool.

Does this calculator give chemical doses?

No. Use the pool volume from this page with the instructions on your product label or ask a pool professional.
